source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check security mode could be enable and work
1. Asserted TPM physical presence by on-board jumper or switch
2. Power on SUT and enter into F1 setup.
3. Navigate to Security page to enable secure boot and TPM function.
4. Install Windows Server 2012/R2 OS. Load RAID controller driver first during installation if there is out-of-box driver support.
5. Install all necessary driver bases on the latest SDL including chipset/NIC/VGA/storage/PCIe devices. Check all drivers be installed without error.
6. Open PowerShell as administrator.
7. Run the command “confirm-SecureBootUEFI” to verify secure boot is enabled.
8. If secure boot is working, “TRUE” will be displayed on the following line. Otherwise “FALSE” will be displayed.
9. Perform standard UEFI and BMC under OS and then reboot SUT
10. Check UEFI system event log and BMC SEL, there is no any warning/error log.
11. Reboot system and check system can boot normally.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1.SUT can install OS, DD and FW successfully with Security boot Enabled
2. CSM disabled and secure boot Standard Mode. And then reboot into OS normal without any warning/error.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: Windows Server ISO + install media; mokutil (for pre-check)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Install OS sheet-A (Secure Boot enabled): install Windows Server with Secure Boot/TPM on the SUT. Agent can pre-check the secure-boot state from OS sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "bootctl status 2>&1 | grep -iE 'secure boot|setup mode'; mokutil --sb-state 2>&1"; the OS install itself needs the Windows ISO + interactive setup (BIOS F1, RAID driver loading) performed by an operator.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the pre-install secure-boot status (SecureBoot state + Setup Mode) so the user confirms CSM disabled / Secure Boot Standard Mode before install; the OS install evidence (drivers without error, confirm-SecureBootUEFI result) is collected by the operator.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: OS install wipes the boot disk; do not auto-run without an approved ISO and backup of the current OS.

original_test_intent: Install the specified Windows Server 2012/R2 image on an approved target with CSM disabled, Secure Boot Standard Mode and TPM enabled, load the required RAID/platform drivers and firmware, verify Secure Boot, inspect UEFI/BMC events and confirm normal reboot.
original_method: An engineer asserts TPM physical presence and configures BIOS; the Windows installer loads the approved RAID driver and installs the OS, drivers and firmware; administrative PowerShell runs Confirm-SecureBootUEFI; management/event evidence and a final reboot establish health.
manual_activity: An engineer must assert the physical-presence control, configure F1 BIOS, confirm the storage target and supervise console recovery. The installation, driver application, PowerShell verification, reboots and evidence collection can be automated with an approved unattended plan.
required_inputs: Exact Windows Server 2012/R2 edition/build, image hash, license and boot media
Dedicated target disk or RAID virtual disk by stable serial/WWN, complete backup and reimage plan
RAID controller identity and signed RAID/chipset/NIC/VGA/storage/PCIe driver and firmware versions
CSM-disabled, Secure Boot Standard Mode, TPM and key-enrollment policy
Defined UEFI/BMC-under-OS checks, expected logs, OOB/KVM and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Never infer or choose the install target; reject mounted, active OS/boot/EFI, swap, LVM, device-mapper, protected or unapproved RAID members.
Verify image and all boot-critical drivers against the exact platform and Secure Boot policy before writes.
Preserve pre-install storage, key and management evidence and recovery credentials; do not clear logs.
Stop on target mismatch, unsigned driver, storage loss, Secure Boot false, POST/boot failure or unexpected management event; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the immutable image, target, driver and security manifest and capture pre-install inventories.
After operator preparation/approval, run the unattended installation and approved driver/firmware sequence once, collecting installer and deployment logs.
Run Confirm-SecureBootUEFI, inventory drivers, inspect UEFI/BMC evidence, perform the approved reboot and report tool results separately from verdict.
engineer_actions: Perform and document physical presence and BIOS configuration.
Approve the exact target, image, signed drivers/firmware and recovery plan.
Review Secure Boot, install, driver, log and boot evidence and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: bootctl and mokutil may support a Linux pre-install environment but cannot prove the installed Windows Secure Boot state, target integrity, driver success or Standard Mode. The source's Confirm-SecureBootUEFI is the relevant Windows check when supported.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain Confirm-SecureBootUEFI with exact PowerShell spelling after install. Build commands only from the approved unattended-install and driver packages; do not invent target or firmware syntax.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Windows Server 2012/R2, RAID-first driver loading, complete SDL driver/firmware coverage, two reboot-related checks and 60/10-minute fields are retained.

modernized_recommendation.status: AUTOMATE DEPLOYMENT ONLY AFTER IMMUTABLE TARGET MANIFEST
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a project-approved unattended Windows deployment tied to the exact disk/array identity and signed driver set; capture setup logs, device status, Confirm-SecureBootUEFI, CSM/Standard Mode evidence, UEFI/BMC events and final reboot health.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only hardware and firmware that support the specified Windows Server 2012/R2 image and driver set.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record the OS build, install media, deployment tooling, every driver/firmware package, BIOS, BMC and TPM version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project/vendor support matrix and signed Windows/RAID deployment procedure; no newer OS is substituted for the source target.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes target selection and install evidence deterministic while retaining the source OS, firmware-security and driver coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No loss; manual physical presence/BIOS and all source post-checks remain.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Image, target, packages, security policy and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An unattended workflow can destroy the wrong disk if stable identity validation is absent.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve another OS image or deployment tool, but that changes the source target and must be recorded as an override with coverage impact. Missing image/target/package inputs are NOT READY, not permanent BLOCKED. Successful project execution does not claim an unexecuted source image also passed.
expected_evidence: Image/hash/license, stable target identity, storage baseline, package manifest, security policy, backup/recovery and approval
Physical-presence and BIOS CSM/Secure Boot Standard/TPM evidence
Installer/partition/RAID/driver/firmware logs and complete Windows device status
Confirm-SecureBootUEFI TRUE, UEFI/BMC/SEL evidence, normal reboot, non-target integrity and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently targets a Secure Boot-enabled Windows install. 'DD and FW' and 'standard UEFI and BMC under OS' require project definitions but do not prescribe incompatible actions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation is understood and can proceed safely after the project supplies exact target, media and packages. V3.1 treats those as readiness rather than a permanent block.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keep PARTIAL but reject its Linux-only pre-check as evidence of the Windows outcome and add stable target/driver controls.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Preserve all destructive storage and firmware gates while changing BLOCKED to NOT READY under locked V3.1.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Defines an automatable install core after manual physical/BIOS preparation and separates tool result from engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Preserves legacy OS coverage while adding exact disk identity, signed package provenance, non-target protection and authoritative Windows Secure Boot evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Physical presence and BIOS setup require an engineer, but the installation and validation core can use an approved unattended workflow. Absent media and target data prevent execution today but do not make the case semantically blocked; therefore PARTIAL is correct.
